subject: POC capacity planning for NovaTech - success criteria & reserved GPU request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@novatech.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@novatech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC capacity planning for NovaTech - success criteria & reserved GPU request

Hi Jordan / Priya -

Thanks again for the call earlier - great alignment on the evaluation goals. As promised, summary + proposed capacity for the POC so we can finalize timelines. Please review and let me know if anything is off.

Quick summary of success criteria (from our convo):
- Functionality: end-to-end integration with NovaTech ingestion, inference, and result storage.
- Quality: extractive summarization F1 >= 0.78 on the sample eval set you shared.
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 1.5s for a 256-token response under POC traffic profile.
- Throughput: sustain baseline of ~30 req/s; handle peak bursts to ~120 req/s.
- Cost/ops: verify we can meet target cost per 1k tokens within the committed POC budget.

Capacity ask (recommended for a 4-week POC):
- Reserved capacity: 4 x A100-style GPUs in a Dedicated pool (guaranteed throughput).
- Autoscaling/burst: allow burst up to 12 GPUs (3x reserved) for short traffic spikes; target cool-down 5m and max burst duration 30m.
- Prewarm/cache: we will prewarm KV cache for your common prefixes and recommend an initial cache TTL of 4 hours during tests.
- Batching: start with small batch window (20 - 40ms) for latency-sensitive flows, increase for throughput tests.

Requested inputs from NovaTech this week:
1) Confirm average request tokens (prompt + response) : you mentioned ~300 tokens average.
2) Provide a 24-hour sample traffic trace (even coarse minute-level rates) so we can model autoscaling.
3) Confirm any regulatory constraints (data residency or retention changes).

Attachments: I attached our capacity estimate workbook (novatech-poc-capacity-estimates.xlsx) and a draft SOW.

Next steps / timeline I propose:
- By Fri 8 May: NovaTech provides sample trace + token averages.
- Mon 11 May: Redwood sends finalized capacity configuration + pricing for reserved and burst usage.
- Wed 13 May: Kickoff and environment prep; POC start Mon 18 May (4 weeks).

Owners: Marissa (sales) - overall POC coordination; Rishi (SE) - infra & tuning; Neha (CS) - onboarding & success metrics.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa - this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Token averages: confirmed ~280 tokens average (prompt+response) for our main summarization flow; exploratory prompts spike to ~600 occasionally.
- Traffic: attaching a coarse 24-hr trace (we'll upload full from platform next). Rough peaks we've seen are 100 - 130 req/s during business hours; baseline overnight ~10 - 15 req/s.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 1.5s for 256-token responses is acceptable as the target. If we see steady >2s we need to escalate.
- Data residency: all POC data can remain in us-west for the trial.

On capacity: we're comfortable starting with 4 reserved GPUs; we want the ability to burst to 10 GPUs. We'll rely on your guidance for batching/caching.

Next: we'll upload the trace and a small eval set (10k samples) into the Drive link you shared by EOD Fri.

Jordan

On Thu, May 7, 2026 at 09:04 AM Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@novatech.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa - this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
>
> - Token averages: confirmed ~280 tokens average (prompt+response) for our main summarization flow; exploratory prompts spike to ~600 occasionally.
> - Traffic: attaching a coarse 24-hr trace...

Thanks - adding technical recommendations for the POC infra based on their numbers: 

1) Reserved: 4 x A100-class GPUs (vRAM and NVLink recommended) as Marissa suggested. That should cover baseline throughput at 30 req/s and typical concurrency given ~280 tokens.
2) Burst/autoscale: allow burst to 10 GPUs (Jordan asked for 10) with scaling policy:
   - Scale-up: when 1-min avg CPU/GPU utilization > 70% or queue length > 40 requests for 90s.
   - Scale-down: cool-down 5m after burst; remove burst nodes after 10m of sustained low utilization.
3) Prewarm & KV cache: we'll prewarm top 50 prefixes and keep KV cache warm for 4 hours; this reduces warm-start latency for repeated sessions.
4) Batching: start with batch window 30ms for low-latency path; for throughput tests we can raise to 150ms.
5) Observability: enable per-route tracing and token-level cost telemetry; we'll add alert for p95 > 1.5s.

A couple of operational notes:
- For short sustained bursts (30 - 45m) we recommend increasing burst allowance to 12 GPUs, but we should keep billing guardrails (max burst minutes per day) to prevent runaway cost.
- Neha - can you confirm we have a CS-runbook for onboarding their eval set and gate criteria for our success dashboard?

I'll turn these into a configuration snippet and attach to the SOW before we finalize pricing.

-rishi
